In the scratch folder all four pass mix format --check-formatted and run against a stand-in Decimal: correct per-currency totals, correct last-order dates (including a +02:00 row that falls on the previous UTC day), the top customers with ties broken by id, and empty results for []. Haiku-1 accepts an unknown status string (it keeps status as an unchecked string) and reports the last order as a DateTime where the prompt asks for a date; haiku-2 raises FunctionClauseError for a non-string amount because parse_amount/1 hands it to Decimal.parse/1. No listed rule covers the last two.

Rules changed since 74112b4 on this case's list, graded against the current text: the `with` rule (failure shape of each step, nil lookups, an else returning one value, the private-function clause for a second call not returning {:ok, value}), the Enum/Map table (new Enum.find_value/2 row), the `do:` rule (an `if` with an `else` takes do ... end unless it fits about 60 characters; function-head guard wrap; checked value left of ==), the `->` rule (renamed from "Inline `->` clauses that read at a glance; otherwise put each body on its own line" and rewritten), and the pipeline rule (new bullet on multi-line steps). The `->` verdict for haiku-1 line 52 is decided by "Neither do bodies of several expressions or a nested construct.": the body {:ok, Enum.map(results, fn {:ok, order} -> order end)} holds a fn. The old text held a body that is one expression simple enough to take in at a glance, so under 74112b4 this line could have been held clean. The same line is also counted under One expression per line (unchanged), since that rule names a fn as a nested construct that goes on the lines below a `->` pattern, and the `do:` rule treats the analogous `defp draws, do: Enum.map(1..5, fn _draw -> :rand.uniform() end)` as a block.

`->` judgements under the new text. The about-70-character limit no longer applies to single-clause fn arguments: "A single-clause `fn` passed as an argument follows the one-expression rule instead: one expression stays on the `fn`'s line, more goes below." So sonnet-1 line 68 (fn clause about 70 characters, line 82 characters after the indentation) is clean without a length judgement. Held as tables, rows that each give an answer: haiku-1 79-81, 87-89, 95-96; haiku-2 37-38 ({:cont, ...} and {:halt, error}, the shape 2026-10-31 held as a table), 69-71, 77-78; sonnet-1 143-144 and 152-153, where {:ok, DateTime.to_date(datetime)} is held as the answer converted, not a row that calls on as hash_if_canonical(token, bytes) does; if that sentence is meant to cover any call in a row, sonnet-1 is violated at line 152. Sonnet-1 line 131 is a one-clause with ... else held clean as a one-row mapping. Sonnet-2 breaks every case body, which the new default asks for.

Pipelines (new bullet "Every step after a `|>` fits on its line"): no run has a pipeline step after a `|>` that spans several lines, and no run has a pipeline whose head is a multi-line case or cond. Pipelines checked: haiku-1 45-47, 101-105, 136-140; haiku-2 89-91, 109-111, 124-128; sonnet-1 66-68, 76-79, 87-91; sonnet-2 89-91, 100-103, 108-110, 116-118, 122-126.
